notes:
• In the desktop app, each ZTC pane's header shows its provider and model, and their menus switch that pane alone or make it the default.
• A Zerg Router provider with no key opens Router's Credentials page from a pane's menu; a key you haven't set is asked for in that pane.
• A ZTC split starts on the provider, model and route of the pane it splits; a new tab still starts on the default for new panes.
• A default saved in one ZTC pane is no longer erased by another pane's save, and desktop panes pick up new keys and logins in seconds.
changes: A model chosen for the main pane alone reaches everything that reads it.
A default saved in one pane is no longer erased by another pane's save.
Restores and the web mirror follow a pane's own switch.
The title bar offers no Queue or Stop for a ZTC pane whose program exited.
A native ZTC pane works as any ZTC pane in the desktop app.
Each ZTC pane in the desktop app has its own provider and model menus.
Choosing a provider that isn't set up asks for what it needs in that pane.
A ZTC split starts on the provider, model and route of the pane it splits
The title bar's model chip switches only the focused pane
A default you choose in a run launched with --provider, --model or --auth-mode applies to the panes it opens.
